verses: قَدْ أَفْلَحَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنُونَ
ٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ فِى صَلَاتِهِمْ خَٰشِعُونَ
وَٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ عَنِ ٱللَّغْوِ مُعْرِضُونَ
وَٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ لِلزَّكَوٰةِ فَٰعِلُونَ
وَٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ لِفُرُوجِهِمْ حَٰفِظُونَ
إِلَّا عَلَىٰٓ أَزْوَٰجِهِمْ أَوْ مَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَٰنُهُمْ فَإِنَّهُمْ غَيْرُ مَلُومِينَ
فَمَنِ ٱبْتَغَىٰ وَرَآءَ ذَٰلِكَ فَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْعَادُونَ
وَٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ لِأَمَٰنَٰتِهِمْ وَعَهْدِهِمْ رَٰعُونَ
وَٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ عَلَىٰ صَلَوَٰتِهِمْ يُحَافِظُونَ
أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْوَٰرِثُونَ
ٱلَّذِينَ يَرِثُونَ ٱلْفِرْدَوْسَ هُمْ فِيهَا خَٰلِدُونَ
وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا ٱلْإِنسَٰنَ مِن سُلَٰلَةٍ مِّن طِينٍ
ثُمَّ جَعَلْنَٰهُ نُطْفَةً فِى قَرَارٍ مَّكِينٍ

ثُمَّ خَلَقْنَا ٱلنُّطْفَةَ عَلَقَةً فَخَلَقْنَا ٱلْعَلَقَةَ مُضْغَةً فَخَلَقْنَا ٱلْمُضْغَةَ عِظَٰمًا فَكَسَوْنَا ٱلْعِظَٰمَ لَحْمًا ثُمَّ أَنشَأْنَٰهُ خَلْقًا ءَاخَرَ فَتَبَارَكَ ٱللَّهُ أَحْسَنُ ٱلْخَٰلِقِينَ
ثُمَّ إِنَّكُم بَعْدَ ذَٰلِكَ لَمَيِّتُونَ
ثُمَّ إِنَّكُمْ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ تُبْعَثُونَ
وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا فَوْقَكُمْ سَبْعَ طَرَآئِقَ وَمَا كُنَّا عَنِ ٱلْخَلْقِ غَٰفِلِينَ
وَأَنزَلْنَا مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءًۢ بِقَدَرٍ فَأَسْكَنَّٰهُ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَإِنَّا عَلَىٰ ذَهَابٍۭ بِهِۦ لَقَٰدِرُونَ
فَأَنشَأْنَا لَكُم بِهِۦ جَنَّٰتٍ مِّن نَّخِيلٍ وَأَعْنَٰبٍ لَّكُمْ فِيهَا فَوَٰكِهُ كَثِيرَةٌ وَمِنْهَا تَأْكُلُونَ
وَشَجَرَةً تَخْرُجُ مِن طُورِ سَيْنَآءَ تَنۢبُتُ بِٱلدُّهْنِ وَصِبْغٍ لِّلْءَاكِلِينَ
وَإِنَّ لَكُمْ فِى ٱلْأَنْعَٰمِ لَعِبْرَةً نُّسْقِيكُم مِّمَّا فِى بُطُونِهَا وَلَكُمْ فِيهَا مَنَٰفِعُ كَثِيرَةٌ وَمِنْهَا تَأْكُلُونَ
وَعَلَيْهَا وَعَلَى ٱلْفُلْكِ تُحْمَلُونَ
وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا نُوحًا إِلَىٰ قَوْمِهِۦ فَقَالَ يَٰقَوْمِ ٱعْبُدُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ مَا لَكُم مِّنْ إِلَٰهٍ غَيْرُهُۥٓ أَفَلَا تَتَّقُونَ

فَقَالَ ٱلْمَلَؤُا۟ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ مِن قَوْمِهِۦ مَا هَٰذَآ إِلَّا بَشَرٌ مِّثْلُكُمْ يُرِيدُ أَن يَتَفَضَّلَ عَلَيْكُمْ وَلَوْ شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ لَأَنزَلَ مَلَٰٓئِكَةً مَّا سَمِعْنَا بِهَٰذَا فِىٓ ءَابَآئِنَا ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ
إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا رَجُلٌۢ بِهِۦ جِنَّةٌ فَتَرَبَّصُوا۟ بِهِۦ حَتَّىٰ حِينٍ
قَالَ رَبِّ ٱنصُرْنِى بِمَا كَذَّبُونِ

فَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَيْهِ أَنِ ٱصْنَعِ ٱلْفُلْكَ بِأَعْيُنِنَا وَوَحْيِنَا فَإِذَا جَآءَ أَمْرُنَا وَفَارَ ٱلتَّنُّورُ فَٱسْلُكْ فِيهَا مِن كُلٍّ زَوْجَيْنِ ٱثْنَيْنِ وَأَهْلَكَ إِلَّا مَن سَبَقَ عَلَيْهِ ٱلْقَوْلُ مِنْهُمْ وَلَا تُخَٰطِبْنِى فِى ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوٓا۟ إِنَّهُم مُّغْرَقُونَ
فَإِذَا ٱسْتَوَيْتَ أَنتَ وَمَن مَّعَكَ عَلَى ٱلْفُلْكِ فَقُلِ ٱلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ ٱلَّذِى نَجَّىٰنَا مِنَ ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
وَقُل رَّبِّ أَنزِلْنِى مُنزَلًا مُّبَارَكًا وَأَنتَ خَيْرُ ٱلْمُنزِلِينَ
إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَءَايَٰتٍ وَإِن كُنَّا لَمُبْتَلِينَ
ثُمَّ أَنشَأْنَا مِنۢ بَعْدِهِمْ قَرْنًا ءَاخَرِينَ
فَأَرْسَلْنَا فِيهِمْ رَسُولًا مِّنْهُمْ أَنِ ٱعْبُدُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ مَا لَكُم مِّنْ إِلَٰهٍ غَيْرُهُۥٓ أَفَلَا تَتَّقُونَ

وَقَالَ ٱلْمَلَأُ مِن قَوْمِهِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ وَكَذَّبُوا۟ بِلِقَآءِ ٱلْءَاخِرَةِ وَأَتْرَفْنَٰهُمْ فِى ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا مَا هَٰذَآ إِلَّا بَشَرٌ مِّثْلُكُمْ يَأْكُلُ مِمَّا تَأْكُلُونَ مِنْهُ وَيَشْرَبُ مِمَّا تَشْرَبُونَ
وَلَئِنْ أَطَعْتُم بَشَرًا مِّثْلَكُمْ إِنَّكُمْ إِذًا لَّخَٰسِرُونَ
أَيَعِدُكُمْ أَنَّكُمْ إِذَا مِتُّمْ وَكُنتُمْ تُرَابًا وَعِظَٰمًا أَنَّكُم مُّخْرَجُونَ
هَيْهَاتَ هَيْهَاتَ لِمَا تُوعَدُونَ
إِنْ هِىَ إِلَّا حَيَاتُنَا ٱلدُّنْيَا نَمُوتُ وَنَحْيَا وَمَا نَحْنُ بِمَبْعُوثِينَ
إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا رَجُلٌ ٱفْتَرَىٰ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ كَذِبًا وَمَا نَحْنُ لَهُۥ بِمُؤْمِنِينَ
قَالَ رَبِّ ٱنصُرْنِى بِمَا كَذَّبُونِ
قَالَ عَمَّا قَلِيلٍ لَّيُصْبِحُنَّ نَٰدِمِينَ
فَأَخَذَتْهُمُ ٱلصَّيْحَةُ بِٱلْحَقِّ فَجَعَلْنَٰهُمْ غُثَآءً فَبُعْدًا لِّلْقَوْمِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
ثُمَّ أَنشَأْنَا مِنۢ بَعْدِهِمْ قُرُونًا ءَاخَرِينَ
مَا تَسْبِقُ مِنْ أُمَّةٍ أَجَلَهَا وَمَا يَسْتَـْٔخِرُونَ
ثُمَّ أَرْسَلْنَا رُسُلَنَا تَتْرَا كُلَّ مَا جَآءَ أُمَّةً رَّسُولُهَا كَذَّبُوهُ فَأَتْبَعْنَا بَعْضَهُم بَعْضًا وَجَعَلْنَٰهُمْ أَحَادِيثَ فَبُعْدًا لِّقَوْمٍ لَّا يُؤْمِنُونَ
ثُمَّ أَرْسَلْنَا مُوسَىٰ وَأَخَاهُ هَٰرُونَ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا وَسُلْطَٰنٍ مُّبِينٍ
إِلَىٰ فِرْعَوْنَ وَمَلَإِي۟هِۦ فَٱسْتَكْبَرُوا۟ وَكَانُوا۟ قَوْمًا عَالِينَ
فَقَالُوٓا۟ أَنُؤْمِنُ لِبَشَرَيْنِ مِثْلِنَا وَقَوْمُهُمَا لَنَا عَٰبِدُونَ
فَكَذَّبُوهُمَا فَكَانُوا۟ مِنَ ٱلْمُهْلَكِينَ
وَلَقَدْ ءَاتَيْنَا مُوسَى ٱلْكِتَٰبَ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَهْتَدُونَ
وَجَعَلْنَا ٱبْنَ مَرْيَمَ وَأُمَّهُۥٓ ءَايَةً وَءَاوَيْنَٰهُمَآ إِلَىٰ رَبْوَةٍ ذَاتِ قَرَارٍ وَمَعِينٍ
يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلرُّسُلُ كُلُوا۟ مِنَ ٱلطَّيِّبَٰتِ وَٱعْمَلُوا۟ صَٰلِحًا إِنِّى بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ عَلِيمٌ
وَإِنَّ هَٰذِهِۦٓ أُمَّتُكُمْ أُمَّةً وَٰحِدَةً وَأَنَا۠ رَبُّكُمْ فَٱتَّقُونِ
فَتَقَطَّعُوٓا۟ أَمْرَهُم بَيْنَهُمْ زُبُرًا كُلُّ حِزْبٍۭ بِمَا لَدَيْهِمْ فَرِحُونَ
فَذَرْهُمْ فِى غَمْرَتِهِمْ حَتَّىٰ حِينٍ
أَيَحْسَبُونَ أَنَّمَا نُمِدُّهُم بِهِۦ مِن مَّالٍ وَبَنِينَ
نُسَارِعُ لَهُمْ فِى ٱلْخَيْرَٰتِ بَل لَّا يَشْعُرُونَ
إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ هُم مِّنْ خَشْيَةِ رَبِّهِم مُّشْفِقُونَ
وَٱلَّذِينَ هُم بِـَٔايَٰتِ رَبِّهِمْ يُؤْمِنُونَ
وَٱلَّذِينَ هُم بِرَبِّهِمْ لَا يُشْرِكُونَ
وَٱلَّذِينَ يُؤْتُونَ مَآ ءَاتَوا۟ وَّقُلُوبُهُمْ وَجِلَةٌ أَنَّهُمْ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِمْ رَٰجِعُونَ
أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ يُسَٰرِعُونَ فِى ٱلْخَيْرَٰتِ وَهُمْ لَهَا سَٰبِقُونَ
وَلَا نُكَلِّفُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا وَلَدَيْنَا كِتَٰبٌ يَنطِقُ بِٱلْحَقِّ وَهُمْ لَا يُظْلَمُونَ
بَلْ قُلُوبُهُمْ فِى غَمْرَةٍ مِّنْ هَٰذَا وَلَهُمْ أَعْمَٰلٌ مِّن دُونِ ذَٰلِكَ هُمْ لَهَا عَٰمِلُونَ
حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَآ أَخَذْنَا مُتْرَفِيهِم بِٱلْعَذَابِ إِذَا هُمْ يَجْـَٔرُونَ
لَا تَجْـَٔرُوا۟ ٱلْيَوْمَ إِنَّكُم مِّنَّا لَا تُنصَرُونَ
قَدْ كَانَتْ ءَايَٰتِى تُتْلَىٰ عَلَيْكُمْ فَكُنتُمْ عَلَىٰٓ أَعْقَٰبِكُمْ تَنكِصُونَ
مُسْتَكْبِرِينَ بِهِۦ سَٰمِرًا تَهْجُرُونَ
أَفَلَمْ يَدَّبَّرُوا۟ ٱلْقَوْلَ أَمْ جَآءَهُم مَّا لَمْ يَأْتِ ءَابَآءَهُمُ ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ
أَمْ لَمْ يَعْرِفُوا۟ رَسُولَهُمْ فَهُمْ لَهُۥ مُنكِرُونَ
أَمْ يَقُولُونَ بِهِۦ جِنَّةٌۢ بَلْ جَآءَهُم بِٱلْحَقِّ وَأَكْثَرُهُمْ لِلْحَقِّ كَٰرِهُونَ
وَلَوِ ٱتَّبَعَ ٱلْحَقُّ أَهْوَآءَهُمْ لَفَسَدَتِ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتُ وَٱلْأَرْضُ وَمَن فِيهِنَّ بَلْ أَتَيْنَٰهُم بِذِكْرِهِمْ فَهُمْ عَن ذِكْرِهِم مُّعْرِضُونَ
أَمْ تَسْـَٔلُهُمْ خَرْجًا فَخَرَاجُ رَبِّكَ خَيْرٌ وَهُوَ خَيْرُ ٱلرَّٰزِقِينَ
وَإِنَّكَ لَتَدْعُوهُمْ إِلَىٰ صِرَٰطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ
وَإِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِٱلْءَاخِرَةِ عَنِ ٱلصِّرَٰطِ لَنَٰكِبُونَ
وَلَوْ رَحِمْنَٰهُمْ وَكَشَفْنَا مَا بِهِم مِّن ضُرٍّ لَّلَجُّوا۟ فِى طُغْيَٰنِهِمْ يَعْمَهُونَ
وَلَقَدْ أَخَذْنَٰهُم بِٱلْعَذَابِ فَمَا ٱسْتَكَانُوا۟ لِرَبِّهِمْ وَمَا يَتَضَرَّعُونَ
حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا فَتَحْنَا عَلَيْهِم بَابًا ذَا عَذَابٍ شَدِيدٍ إِذَا هُمْ فِيهِ مُبْلِسُونَ
وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِىٓ أَنشَأَ لَكُمُ ٱلسَّمْعَ وَٱلْأَبْصَٰرَ وَٱلْأَفْـِٔدَةَ قَلِيلًا مَّا تَشْكُرُونَ
وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِى ذَرَأَكُمْ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَإِلَيْهِ تُحْشَرُونَ
وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِى يُحْىِۦ وَيُمِيتُ وَلَهُ ٱخْتِلَٰفُ ٱلَّيْلِ وَٱلنَّهَارِ أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ
بَلْ قَالُوا۟ مِثْلَ مَا قَالَ ٱلْأَوَّلُونَ
قَالُوٓا۟ أَءِذَا مِتْنَا وَكُنَّا تُرَابًا وَعِظَٰمًا أَءِنَّا لَمَبْعُوثُونَ
لَقَدْ وُعِدْنَا نَحْنُ وَءَابَآؤُنَا هَٰذَا مِن قَبْلُ إِنْ هَٰذَآ إِلَّآ أَسَٰطِيرُ ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ
قُل لِّمَنِ ٱلْأَرْضُ وَمَن فِيهَآ إِن كُنتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ
سَيَقُولُونَ لِلَّهِ قُلْ أَفَلَا تَذَكَّرُونَ

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/ane-quran/22-ane-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: God makes the fluid (seed) in women into a human and forms the child in its mother's belly (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in Great Hymn to the Aten - the god makes seed grow in women, nurses the child in the womb, gives breath to the chick in the egg; 'O sole god, there is no other' (AtenHymn 6/3-7/7): The god gives breath to the chick in the egg and sets its time to break out and walk; The god gives breath to keep alive all that he has made; When the child comes forth from the womb the god opens its mouth and supplies its needs; Exclamation of praise: how many (how excellent) are the things you have made; God formed the kidneys and wove (knit) the speaker in his mother's womb; Declaration that YHWH is God and there is no other besides him.

matches.note: Ur-Namma, with no god to help him, says 'just as the rain pouring down from heaven cannot turn back, alas, nor can I turn back to brick-built Urim' (1:164-165). The dying man of 23:99-100 asks 'my Lord, send me back, that I may do right in what I left', and is refused: 'no! ... and behind them is a barrier (barzakh) until the day they are raised'. Ur-Namma wants to go back to his city; the Quranic man wants to go back to do good. Both are refused; in the Quran the refusal lasts only until the resurrection.

Only in Against the false prophets and the women who hunt souls: False prophets will not be in the council of God's people nor written in the register of the house of Israel; The prophets of Israel are like foxes (jackals) among ruins; Diviners profane God for handfuls of barley and crumbs of bread; False prophets mislead the people saying 'Peace' when there is no peace; The true prophet's task is to go up into the breaches and build a wall for the people on the day of battle; false prophets did not; God tears off the magic bands and lets the trapped souls go free 'like birds' (leporhot); Parable: one who builds on the brink of a crumbling bank falls with it into hell; None more wrong than one who falsely claims revelation or says he can send down the like of God's; False prophets daub a flimsy wall with whitewash (tafel); God's storm, flood-rain and hailstones bring it down; Women prophetesses sew bands (kesatot) on wrists and make veils (mispahot) for heads to hunt souls, killing and keeping alive by magic; Kings or people practice divination (qesem) and augury (nihush); God casts great hailstones from heaven, killing more than the sword; and 2 more.

Only in One community split into sects; the heedless rich and the God-fearing: Nation pictured as a body beaten from sole of foot to head, with untended wounds and sores; Humanity was one community (umma) but split its affair into sects; Were there gods besides God in heaven and earth, both would have been ruined; Refrain listing plagues (famine, drought, blight, locust, pestilence, war, overthrow): 'yet you did not return to me'; God did not send the prophets who promise peace; they prophesy a lying vision, divination and the deceit of their heart; God burdens no soul beyond its capacity; Speaker is troubled by the prosperity and ease of the wicked (theodicy); Officers call the visiting prophet 'this madman' (meshugga'); The Prophet asks no wage for the message; God keeps a book in which names are written and from which sinners are blotted.

leads.title: The valley of dry bones ↔ Man from clay through the stages of the womb; seven paths, water, Sinai's tree, cattle and ships
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: In the womb God makes the lump into bones and clothes the bones with flesh, then makes it another creation (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in The valley of dry bones: God will open his people's graves, bring them up from their graves and bring them to the land of Israel; The exiles say 'Our bones are dried up, our hope is lost, we are cut off'; The prophet summons the breath (ruah) from the four winds to breathe into the slain so they live; The prophet is set down in a valley full of very many, very dry bones and led around among them; God asks 'Can these bones live?' and the prophet answers 'Lord God, you know'; The revived dead stand on their feet, an exceedingly great army; God will put his own spirit within them and cause them to walk in his statutes; A multitude of dead revived [divergence between the texts]; The question whether God can make the dead live [divergence between the texts]; The question whether dead bones can live again, and who asks it [divergence between the texts]; A single cry or rebuke (zajra) and the dead stand looking; At the prophet's word there is a rattling; bones come together bone to bone, then sinews, flesh and skin cover them, but there is no breath; and 3 more.

Only in Man from clay through the stages of the womb; seven paths, water, Sinai's tree, cattle and ships: God called 'the best of creators' (aḥsan al-khāliqīn); Cattle are a lesson: God gives drink from what is in their bellies; A tree springing from Mount Sinai (Ṭūr Saynāʾ) yields oil and a relish for eaters; God's crafting of the human body, and what is said to follow from it [divergence between the texts]; Man is made from compacted (clotted) blood and then bones; God makes the fluid (seed) in women into a human and forms the child in its mother's belly; At creation God fixed the weight of the wind, the measure of the waters, a decree for the rain and a way for the thunderbolt; Humans created from dust, then a drop (nuṭfa), then a clinging clot (ʿalaqa), then a chewed lump (muḍgha), shaped and unshaped; God's eyes saw the speaker's unformed substance (golem); all his days were written in God's book before one of them existed; God poured the embryo out like milk and curdled it like cheese, clothing it with skin and flesh and knitting bones and sinews; God fashions seven heavens; The speaker too was 'pinched off from clay' (qoratsti), like a figure nipped from a lump of clay; and 1 more.

leads.title: Second creation account, Eden, and the making of woman ↔ Man from clay through the stages of the womb; seven paths, water, Sinai's tree, cattle and ships

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: First human shaped from dust, clay or soil (weight 5.2). Pair score 5.2.

Only in Second creation account, Eden, and the making of woman: Eating the forbidden fruit is threatened with death; The first human is put in the garden to work and guard it; God made a covenant with Adam, but he forgot and lacked resolve [divergence between the texts]; Whether the first couple were naked or clothed before the fall [contrast between the texts]; The first man and the names of the creatures [divergence between the texts]; How the first human's mate is made from the first human [divergence between the texts]; Whether any fruit in the Garden is forbidden [contrast between the texts]; The tree forbidden to the first humans [divergence between the texts]; Forming a creature from earth and breathing life into it [divergence between the texts]; Four rivers in the Garden [divergence between the texts]; The garden given to the first humans to live and eat in [divergence between the texts]; In the garden Adam will not hunger, be naked, thirst or suffer the sun's heat [divergence between the texts]; and 21 more.

Only in Man from clay through the stages of the womb; seven paths, water, Sinai's tree, cattle and ships: God called 'the best of creators' (aḥsan al-khāliqīn); Cattle are a lesson: God gives drink from what is in their bellies; A tree springing from Mount Sinai (Ṭūr Saynāʾ) yields oil and a relish for eaters; In the womb God makes the lump into bones and clothes the bones with flesh, then makes it another creation; God's crafting of the human body, and what is said to follow from it [divergence between the texts]; Man is made from compacted (clotted) blood and then bones; God makes the fluid (seed) in women into a human and forms the child in its mother's belly; At creation God fixed the weight of the wind, the measure of the waters, a decree for the rain and a way for the thunderbolt; Humans created from dust, then a drop (nuṭfa), then a clinging clot (ʿalaqa), then a chewed lump (muḍgha), shaped and unshaped; God's eyes saw the speaker's unformed substance (golem); all his days were written in God's book before one of them existed; God poured the embryo out like milk and curdled it like cheese, clothing it with skin and flesh and knitting bones and sinews; God fashions seven heavens; and 1 more.

leads.title: The Flood (full read) ↔ Noah called a madman; the ark and the boiling oven
leads.summary: 7 correspondences read side by side: 5 deliberately changed, 2 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: When and from where the flood waters come [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); What the flood hero does when the vessel comes to rest [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); Whether the flood hero speaks to his people before the flood [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.3); Why God destroyed a generation or a people [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.1); Who is saved with the hero from the destruction, and why [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.8); Animals taken aboard in pairs (weight 6.5); Hero builds a vessel on divine instruction (weight 6.2); Hero's family saved with him (weight 5.4). Pair score 54.9.

Only in The Flood (full read): Clean animals taken aboard by sevens, unclean by pairs; Flood events given exact calendar dates (year of hero's life, month, day); Rain or flood lasts forty days and forty nights; A dove returns with an olive leaf in its beak; Seven days pass between the warning or boarding and the onset of the flood; Angels object that the new human will corrupt the earth and shed blood while they praise God; When the water overflowed God carried 'you' in the running ship (al-jariya) as a reminder for retaining ears [divergence between the texts]; What sets the flood in motion: God's decision on violence, or the rejected prophet's prayer [divergence between the texts]; How the ark is described [divergence between the texts]; What God says of later generations after the flood: no repeat, or punishment to come [contrast between the texts]; How the flood waters are stopped and subside [divergence between the texts]; God made Noah's descendants the only survivors; and 38 more.

Only in Noah called a madman; the ark and the boiling oven: God forbids the prophet to address him on behalf of those who did wrong: they will be drowned; The flood hero prays to be landed at a blessed landing place; The flood hero is told he is only a man like the speaker(s) [divergence between the texts]; The prophet's people object that he is only a human like them; had God willed he would have sent angels; The flood waters are hot or boiling; A member of the hero's family is lost; A specific sign marks the moment to board; Hero asks the deity to judge or destroy his opponents; Hero warns or preaches to his people before the flood; Officers call the visiting prophet 'this madman' (meshugga').

matches.label: Whether the flood hero speaks to his people before the flood
matches.note: In Genesis Noah never speaks before the flood: wa-yyaʿaś Nōaḥ kə-khōl ʾăšer ṣiwwâ ʾōtô; he is chosen because God saw him righteous (ʾōtəkā rāʾîtî ṣaddîq). In the Quran he is a messenger (arsalnā Nūḥan ilā qawmihi) who preaches 'yā qawmi ʿbudū llāha mā lakum min ilāhin ghayruhu', and the chiefs answer that he is only a man like them, possessed (bihi jinna).

passages.text: וַיַּ֖עַשׂ נֹ֑חַ כְּ֠כֹל אֲשֶׁ֨ר צִוָּ֥ה אֹת֛וֹ אֱלֹהִ֖ים כֵּ֥ן עָשָֽׂה
וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ לְנֹ֔חַ בֹּֽא אַתָּ֥ה וְכָל בֵּיתְךָ֖ אֶל הַתֵּבָ֑ה כִּֽי אֹתְךָ֥ רָאִ֛יתִי צַדִּ֥יק לְפָנַ֖י בַּדּ֥וֹר הַזֶּֽה
وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا نُوحًا إِلَىٰ قَوْمِهِۦ فَقَالَ يَٰقَوْمِ ٱعْبُدُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ مَا لَكُم مِّنْ إِلَٰهٍ غَيْرُهُۥٓ أَفَلَا تَتَّقُونَ

فَقَالَ ٱلْمَلَؤُا۟ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ مِن قَوْمِهِۦ مَا هَٰذَآ إِلَّا بَشَرٌ مِّثْلُكُمْ يُرِيدُ أَن يَتَفَضَّلَ عَلَيْكُمْ وَلَوْ شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ لَأَنزَلَ مَلَٰٓئِكَةً مَّا سَمِعْنَا بِهَٰذَا فِىٓ ءَابَآئِنَا ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ
إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا رَجُلٌۢ بِهِۦ جِنَّةٌ فَتَرَبَّصُوا۟ بِهِۦ حَتَّىٰ حِينٍ

matches.label: Why God destroyed a generation or a people
matches.note: Cause of the flood: Gen 6:13 kî mālʾâ hā-ʾāreṣ ḥāmās, the earth filled with violence, and God's own decision (hinnî mašḥîtām); Q 23:26-27: they are drowned for rejecting the messenger (bimā kadhdhabūni ... alladhīna ẓalamū innahum mughraqūn), and Noah asks for it (rabbi nṣurnī).

passages.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֜ים לְנֹ֗חַ קֵ֤ץ כָּל בָּשָׂר֙ בָּ֣א לְפָנַ֔י כִּֽי מָלְאָ֥ה הָאָ֛רֶץ חָמָ֖ס מִפְּנֵיהֶ֑ם וְהִנְנִ֥י מַשְׁחִיתָ֖ם אֶת הָאָֽרֶץ

فَقَالَ ٱلْمَلَؤُا۟ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ مِن قَوْمِهِۦ مَا هَٰذَآ إِلَّا بَشَرٌ مِّثْلُكُمْ يُرِيدُ أَن يَتَفَضَّلَ عَلَيْكُمْ وَلَوْ شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ لَأَنزَلَ مَلَٰٓئِكَةً مَّا سَمِعْنَا بِهَٰذَا فِىٓ ءَابَآئِنَا ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ
قَالَ رَبِّ ٱنصُرْنِى بِمَا كَذَّبُونِ

فَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَيْهِ أَنِ ٱصْنَعِ ٱلْفُلْكَ بِأَعْيُنِنَا وَوَحْيِنَا فَإِذَا جَآءَ أَمْرُنَا وَفَارَ ٱلتَّنُّورُ فَٱسْلُكْ فِيهَا مِن كُلٍّ زَوْجَيْنِ ٱثْنَيْنِ وَأَهْلَكَ إِلَّا مَن سَبَقَ عَلَيْهِ ٱلْقَوْلُ مِنْهُمْ وَلَا تُخَٰطِبْنِى فِى ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوٓا۟ إِنَّهُم مُّغْرَقُونَ

matches.label: When and from where the flood waters come
matches.note: Signal and source: Genesis gives a time (lə-yāmîm ʿôd šivʿâ ʾānōkhî mamṭîr) and waters from the burst springs of the deep and the windows of heaven (nivqəʿû kol maʿyənôt təhôm rabbâ wa-ʾărubbōt haš-šāmayim niftāḥû); the Quran gives a sign, 'when our command comes and the oven boils' (wa-fāra t-tannūr). cf. b. Sanh. 108b (boiling flood waters), outside the HB.

passages.text: כִּי֩ לְיָמִ֨ים ע֜וֹד שִׁבְעָ֗ה אָֽנֹכִי֙ מַמְטִ֣יר עַל הָאָ֔רֶץ אַרְבָּעִ֣ים י֔וֹם וְאַרְבָּעִ֖ים לָ֑יְלָה וּמָחִ֗יתִי אֶֽת כָּל הַיְקוּם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֔יתִי מֵעַ֖ל פְּנֵ֥י הָֽאֲדָמָֽה

בִּשְׁנַ֨ת שֵׁשׁ מֵא֤וֹת שָׁנָה֙ לְחַיֵּי נֹ֔חַ בַּחֹ֨דֶשׁ֙ הַשֵּׁנִ֔י בְּשִׁבְעָֽה עָשָׂ֥ר י֖וֹם לַחֹ֑דֶשׁ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֗ה נִבְקְעוּ֙ כָּֽל מַעְיְנֹת֙ תְּה֣וֹם רַבָּ֔ה וַאֲרֻבֹּ֥ת הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם נִפְתָּֽחוּ

فَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَيْهِ أَنِ ٱصْنَعِ ٱلْفُلْكَ بِأَعْيُنِنَا وَوَحْيِنَا فَإِذَا جَآءَ أَمْرُنَا وَفَارَ ٱلتَّنُّورُ فَٱسْلُكْ فِيهَا مِن كُلٍّ زَوْجَيْنِ ٱثْنَيْنِ وَأَهْلَكَ إِلَّا مَن سَبَقَ عَلَيْهِ ٱلْقَوْلُ مِنْهُمْ وَلَا تُخَٰطِبْنِى فِى ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوٓا۟ إِنَّهُم مُّغْرَقُونَ

matches.label: Who is saved with the hero from the destruction, and why
matches.note: Genesis saves the whole household, bōʾ ʾattâ wə-khol bêtəkā ... Nōaḥ û-vānāyw wə-ʾištô û-nəšê vānāyw; the Quran excepts some: wa-ahlaka illā man sabaqa ʿalayhi l-qawlu minhum (the drowned son of 11:42-43), and forbids Noah to plead for the wrongdoers (wa-lā tukhāṭibnī fī lladhīna ẓalamū).

passages.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ לְנֹ֔חַ בֹּֽא אַתָּ֥ה וְכָל בֵּיתְךָ֖ אֶל הַתֵּבָ֑ה כִּֽי אֹתְךָ֥ רָאִ֛יתִי צַדִּ֥יק לְפָנַ֖י בַּדּ֥וֹר הַזֶּֽה
וַיָּ֣בֹא נֹ֗חַ וּ֠בָנָיו וְאִשְׁתּ֧וֹ וּנְשֵֽׁי בָנָ֛יו אִתּ֖וֹ אֶל הַתֵּבָ֑ה מִפְּנֵ֖י מֵ֥י הַמַּבּֽוּל

فَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَيْهِ أَنِ ٱصْنَعِ ٱلْفُلْكَ بِأَعْيُنِنَا وَوَحْيِنَا فَإِذَا جَآءَ أَمْرُنَا وَفَارَ ٱلتَّنُّورُ فَٱسْلُكْ فِيهَا مِن كُلٍّ زَوْجَيْنِ ٱثْنَيْنِ وَأَهْلَكَ إِلَّا مَن سَبَقَ عَلَيْهِ ٱلْقَوْلُ مِنْهُمْ وَلَا تُخَٰطِبْنِى فِى ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوٓا۟ إِنَّهُم مُّغْرَقُونَ

matches.label: What the flood hero does when the vessel comes to rest
matches.note: End of the voyage: Genesis has the ark resting on the mountains of Ararat, an altar and burnt offerings whose odor God smells, then his promise never again to curse the ground (wa-yyiven Nōaḥ mizbēaḥ ... wa-yyāraḥ YHWH ʾet rêaḥ han-nîḥōaḥ ... lōʾ ʾōsif). The Quran has no altar, sacrifice or promise: Noah says al-ḥamdu lillāhi lladhī najjānā and prays rabbi anzilnī munzalan mubārakan, and the landing place is not named.

passages.text: וַתָּ֤נַח הַתֵּבָה֙ בַּחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔י בְּשִׁבְעָה עָשָׂ֥ר י֖וֹם לַחֹ֑דֶשׁ עַ֖ל הָרֵ֥י אֲרָרָֽט
וַיִּ֥בֶן נֹ֛חַ מִזְבֵּ֖חַ לַֽיהוָ֑ה וַיִּקַּ֞ח מִכֹּ֣ל הַבְּהֵמָ֣ה הַטְּהוֹרָ֗ה וּמִכֹּל֙ הָע֣וֹף הַטָּהֹ֔ר וַיַּ֥עַל עֹלֹ֖ת בַּמִּזְבֵּֽחַ

فَإِذَا ٱسْتَوَيْتَ أَنتَ وَمَن مَّعَكَ عَلَى ٱلْفُلْكِ فَقُلِ ٱلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ ٱلَّذِى نَجَّىٰنَا مِنَ ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
وَقُل رَّبِّ أَنزِلْنِى مُنزَلًا مُّبَارَكًا وَأَنتَ خَيْرُ ٱلْمُنزِلِينَ

leads.title: Hear, O heavens; the great indictment, sacrifice rejected, the faithful city ↔ One community split into sects; the heedless rich and the God-fearing
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Nation pictured as a body beaten from sole of foot to head, with untended wounds and sores (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in Hear, O heavens; the great indictment, sacrifice rejected, the faithful city: City or people given a new name in the future age (e.g. 'City of Righteousness', 'Hephzibah'); The faithful city has become a harlot; silver turned to dross, wine diluted with water; Worshippers shamed by the sacred oaks (elim) and gardens they chose; Daughter Zion left alone like a booth in a vineyard, a hut in a cucumber field, a besieged city; Sky and earth 'listen to their Lord' (adhinat) and are made to obey at the end; Israel likened to a donkey that knows, or does not understand, what it has [divergence between the texts]; Prophet addresses his own rulers and people as 'Sodom' and 'Gomorrah'; In Lot's town only one house of submitters (muslimin) was found, and the believers were brought out; Book or oracle opens with a heading naming the prophet, his father and the kings in whose days he saw the vision; God's people as sons he reared who rebelled against him; Though sins be like scarlet they shall be white as snow; though red as crimson, like wool; God will smelt away the dross of his people as in a furnace to purify them; and 12 more.

Only in One community split into sects; the heedless rich and the God-fearing: Humanity was one community (umma) but split its affair into sects; Whether a prophet takes payment for his message [contrast between the texts]; Were there gods besides God in heaven and earth, both would have been ruined; False prophets prophesy 'from their own heart', following their own spirit, having seen nothing; Refrain listing plagues (famine, drought, blight, locust, pestilence, war, overthrow): 'yet you did not return to me'; God did not send the prophets who promise peace; they prophesy a lying vision, divination and the deceit of their heart; God burdens no soul beyond its capacity; Speaker is troubled by the prosperity and ease of the wicked (theodicy); Officers call the visiting prophet 'this madman' (meshugga'); The Prophet asks no wage for the message; God keeps a book in which names are written and from which sinners are blotted.

leads.title: Song of the strong city; your dead shall live ↔ Repel evil with good; the deathbed plea, the barzakh and the scales
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Your dead shall live, their corpses rise; dwellers in the dust shall awake and sing (weight 6.0). Pair score 6.0.

Only in Song of the strong city; your dead shall live: Other lords ruled us; they are dead, they will not live; shades (rephaim) will not rise; their memory is wiped out; God's dew is a 'dew of lights' (tal orot) and the earth will give birth to the shades (rephaim); The earth will disclose the blood shed on it and no longer cover its slain; 'Go, my people, enter your chambers and shut the doors behind you; hide a little moment until the wrath passes'; We were pregnant, we writhed, but gave birth only to wind; we brought no salvation to the earth; God keeps the steadfast mind in perfect peace (shalom shalom) because it trusts in him; 'My soul yearns for you in the night; my spirit within me seeks you at dawn'; 'We have a strong city... Open the gates that the righteous nation that keeps faith may enter'; In Yah YHWH is an everlasting rock (tsur olamim); What the dead say when they wake from the dust [divergence between the texts]; The Gardens of Eden have their gates opened for the righteous; God lets the people discover the sleepers so they know his promise of resurrection is true; and 7 more.

Only in Repel evil with good; the deathbed plea, the barzakh and the scales: Behind the dead is a barrier (barzakh) until the day they are raised; The damned had taken the believers as a laughingstock; now the believers triumph; God tells the damned pleading to leave hell: 'Be driven away into it and do not speak to me'; At death the sinner begs 'My Lord, send me back, that I may do good'; it is refused; When the trumpet is blown there will be no ties of kinship between them, nor will they ask after one another; Seek refuge in God from the goadings of the devils and from their presence; The dead cannot come back to life on earth; A dying person's plea to God for more life, and God's answer [contrast between the texts]; Whether those who die and return to dust rise again [divergence between the texts]; On that day a great shofar will be blown and the lost in Assyria and outcasts in Egypt will come and worship on the holy mountain; A span of many years is set against a single day [divergence between the texts]; At the judgment after death a whole lifetime is reckoned as an hour or a day; and 10 more.

leads.title: Leviathan slain; the vineyard of delight; the great shofar ↔ Repel evil with good; the deathbed plea, the barzakh and the scales
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: On that day a great shofar will be blown and the lost in Assyria and outcasts in Egypt will come and worship on the holy mountain (weight 7.7); The trumpet (ṣūr) is blown and the dead are gathered (weight 6.0). Pair score 13.8.

Only in Leviathan slain; the vineyard of delight; the great shofar: Jacob's guilt is atoned by making all altar stones like crushed chalk, no Asherim or incense-stands standing; Jacob will take root, Israel blossom and bud and fill the face of the world with fruit; God threshes from the Euphrates to the Wadi of Egypt and the Israelites are gathered one by one; Song of the pleasant vineyard that YHWH guards, waters every moment and keeps night and day; he has no wrath, but would burn its briars; A horn blown on the last day, and whom it gathers [divergence between the texts]; Israel is a vine brought out of Egypt and planted, whose hedges God has broken down; Leviathan, the great sea monster, named; YHWH with his hard, great, strong sword will punish Leviathan the fleeing serpent, Leviathan the twisting serpent, and slay the dragon (tannin) in the sea; Hammanim (incense altars or sun pillars) removed from the cities; God will gather the exiles even from the end of heaven and restore them; Sea, deep or sea monster subdued or defeated by God.

Only in Repel evil with good; the deathbed plea, the barzakh and the scales: Behind the dead is a barrier (barzakh) until the day they are raised; The damned had taken the believers as a laughingstock; now the believers triumph; God tells the damned pleading to leave hell: 'Be driven away into it and do not speak to me'; At death the sinner begs 'My Lord, send me back, that I may do good'; it is refused; When the trumpet is blown there will be no ties of kinship between them, nor will they ask after one another; Seek refuge in God from the goadings of the devils and from their presence; The dead cannot come back to life on earth; A dying person's plea to God for more life, and God's answer [contrast between the texts]; Whether those who die and return to dust rise again [divergence between the texts]; A span of many years is set against a single day [divergence between the texts]; At the judgment after death a whole lifetime is reckoned as an hour or a day; The dead cannot go back to the life they left [divergence between the texts]; and 9 more.

leads.title: Hezekiah's illness, the shadow on the steps of Ahaz, and Hezekiah's psalm ↔ Repel evil with good; the deathbed plea, the barzakh and the scales
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 opposite ruling.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: A dying person's plea to God for more life, and God's answer [contrast between the texts] (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in Hezekiah's illness, the shadow on the steps of Ahaz, and Hezekiah's psalm: Speaker laments that in the noon of his days he must go to the gates of Sheol, deprived of the rest of his years; A psalm-like 'writing' (mikhtav) of the king composed when he was sick and recovered; My dwelling is pulled up like a shepherd's tent; I have rolled up my life like a weaver, he cuts me off from the loom; God has cast all the speaker's sins behind his back and held back his soul from the pit of destruction; The dead cannot praise God: no wonders for the dead, no hesed in the grave, no faithfulness in Abaddon; A cake of figs laid on a boil heals the king; Given a choice of signs, the king picks the harder (shadow going backward); Prophet tells the sick king 'Set your house in order, for you shall die'; Dying man turns his face to the wall and prays, weeping; On that day neither wealth nor sons avail, only one who comes to God with a sound heart; Bequest (wasiyya) to parents and kin prescribed for one who leaves wealth; altering it is a sin; In answer to prayer God adds fifteen years to the king's life; and 5 more.

Shared motifs, rarest first: 'To whom will you liken God, what likeness compare to him?' (weight 7.1). Pair score 7.1.

Only in Comfort my people; a voice in the wilderness; to whom will you liken God: 'Comfort, comfort my people': Jerusalem's term of service is ended and she has received double for her sins; God tends his flock like a shepherd, gathers the lambs in his arm and carries them in his bosom; God brings out the starry host by number and calls each by name; none is missing; God sits enthroned above the circle (hug) of the earth; its inhabitants are like grasshoppers; Nations are like a drop from a bucket and dust on the scales; Lebanon is not enough fuel nor its beasts enough for a burnt offering; A voice cries: 'In the wilderness clear the way of YHWH, make straight in the desert a highway for our God'; Who measured the waters in the hollow of his hand, marked off heaven with a span and weighed the mountains in scales?; God made everything grow in due weight and sends it down only in known measure; A double portion (k-p-l) from God [divergence between the texts]; On the Day of Resurrection the whole earth is in God's grip and the heavens folded in his right hand; A herald of good news (mevasseret Tsiyyon) goes up on a high mountain to announce 'Behold your God!'; Satire on the making of idols: craftsman casts, goldsmith overlays, the poor choose wood that will not rot so the idol will not totter; and 18 more.

Only in Who owns the earth? evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: God did not send the prophets who promise peace; they prophesy a lying vision, divination and the deceit of their heart (weight 6.6). Pair score 6.6.

Only in Concerning the prophets - who has stood in the council of YHWH?: The prophet's heart is broken and all his bones shake; he is like a drunken man because of God's holy words; The prophets of Jerusalem commit adultery and strengthen evildoers; they have become like Sodom and Gomorrah; Whether a prophet has first-hand knowledge of the heavenly council [contrast between the texts]; Whether a prophet speaks from his own heart or desire, or by revelation [contrast between the texts]; The earth mourns and the heavens above grow dark because of God's decree; God gives his people poisoned water (mei rosh) to drink and wormwood to eat; 'Have you listened in the council (sod) of God, and limited wisdom to yourself?'; Prophets and priests heal the wound lightly, saying 'Peace, peace' when there is no peace; Opponents nearly lure the prophet into inventing something else; God makes him firm; The tree of Zaqqum grows from the bottom of hell; its spathes are like the heads of devils; the damned fill their bellies and drink boiling water; The storm of YHWH's fury goes out and whirls on the head of the wicked; in the latter days you will understand it; God enthroned with the host of heaven standing at his right and left deliberates.

Only in One community split into sects; the heedless rich and the God-fearing: Nation pictured as a body beaten from sole of foot to head, with untended wounds and sores; Humanity was one community (umma) but split its affair into sects; Whether a prophet takes payment for his message [contrast between the texts]; Were there gods besides God in heaven and earth, both would have been ruined; False prophets prophesy 'from their own heart', following their own spirit, having seen nothing; Refrain listing plagues (famine, drought, blight, locust, pestilence, war, overthrow): 'yet you did not return to me'; God burdens no soul beyond its capacity; Speaker is troubled by the prosperity and ease of the wicked (theodicy); Officers call the visiting prophet 'this madman' (meshugga'); The Prophet asks no wage for the message; God keeps a book in which names are written and from which sinners are blotted.

leads.title: Job - 'Your hands fashioned me'; land of darkness ↔ Man from clay through the stages of the womb; seven paths, water, Sinai's tree, cattle and ships
leads.summary: 2 correspondences read side by side: 1 deliberately changed, 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: God's crafting of the human body, and what is said to follow from it [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); God poured the embryo out like milk and curdled it like cheese, clothing it with skin and flesh and knitting bones and sinews (weight 6.8); First human shaped from dust, clay or soil (weight 5.2). Pair score 19.8.

Only in Job - 'Your hands fashioned me'; land of darkness: The sufferer reminds God that God's hands shaped him yet now destroy him; 'Have you eyes of flesh? Are your days like a mortal's days?'; God hunts the sufferer like a lion; God created Adam 'with my two hands'; God creates you in your mothers' bellies creation after creation in three darknesses; From dust, then a drop, then a clinging clot ('alaqa), then a child, then full strength, then old age; some die before; Have you seen what you emit? Do you create it, or are we the creator?; Sufferer wishes he had died in the womb or been a hidden stillborn; The underworld as a land of darkness and deep shadow, without order, where light is like darkness; Like a vanishing cloud, whoever goes down to Sheol does not come up; his place knows him no more; Human created in stages: a drop of sperm (nutfa), a clinging clot ('alaq/'alaqa), then shaped and proportioned; Human comes from dust and returns to dust.

Only in Man from clay through the stages of the womb; seven paths, water, Sinai's tree, cattle and ships: God called 'the best of creators' (aḥsan al-khāliqīn); Cattle are a lesson: God gives drink from what is in their bellies; A tree springing from Mount Sinai (Ṭūr Saynāʾ) yields oil and a relish for eaters; In the womb God makes the lump into bones and clothes the bones with flesh, then makes it another creation; Man is made from compacted (clotted) blood and then bones; God makes the fluid (seed) in women into a human and forms the child in its mother's belly; At creation God fixed the weight of the wind, the measure of the waters, a decree for the rain and a way for the thunderbolt; Humans created from dust, then a drop (nuṭfa), then a clinging clot (ʿalaqa), then a chewed lump (muḍgha), shaped and unshaped; God's eyes saw the speaker's unformed substance (golem); all his days were written in God's book before one of them existed; God fashions seven heavens; The speaker too was 'pinched off from clay' (qoratsti), like a figure nipped from a lump of clay.

leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Human comes from dust and returns to dust (weight 5.9). Pair score 5.9.

Only in Elihu - God cannot do wrong: God shows no partiality to princes, nor regards the rich above the poor, for all are the work of his hands; God shatters the mighty without inquiry and sets others in their place; God keeps a godless man from ruling, that he not ensnare the people; If God gathered his spirit and breath to himself, all flesh would perish together and return to dust; Elihu wishes that Job be tried to the end for answering like wicked men; In a moment they die; at midnight people are shaken and pass away, the mighty removed without a hand; 'Does God pervert justice, does Shaddai pervert right?'; Man is abominable and corrupt, drinking iniquity like water; 'Does not the ear test words as the palate tastes food?'; The sufferer is accused of multiplying words without knowledge; God takes the souls at death and of those not dead in their sleep; he keeps those decreed to die and sends back the others for a set term; 'Can a man be of use to God? Is it gain to Shaddai if you are righteous?'; and 3 more.

Only in A later generation's messenger, the Cry, and messengers in succession: God sent his messengers one after another; each was denied and each nation became a tale; A people is seized by the Cry (al-ṣayḥa) and made like flood-scum; Whether those who die and return to dust rise again [contrast between the texts]; Earlier messengers were only men who ate food and were not immortal; Hero asks the deity to judge or destroy his opponents; Your dead shall live, their corpses rise; dwellers in the dust shall awake and sing; Destruction follows the people's rejection of a messenger.

leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Whether those who die and return to dust rise again [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in Job - human life as hard service; 'Am I Sea or Dragon?': Life's days are swifter than a weaver's shuttle; The sufferer's flesh is clothed with worms and clods of dust; his skin cracks and festers; God called 'watcher of humankind' (notser ha'adam) who targets the sufferer; 'What is man that you make so much of him?' turned into a complaint against divine scrutiny (cf. Ps 8); Sufferer says God will seek him in the morning and he will be no more; Human life on earth is hard service (tsava), its days like those of a hired laborer; 'Am I Sea, or the Dragon (tannin), that you set a guard over me?'; God terrifies the sufferer with dreams and visions at night; Like a vanishing cloud, whoever goes down to Sheol does not come up; his place knows him no more; Sea, deep or sea monster subdued or defeated by God.

Only in Repel evil with good; the deathbed plea, the barzakh and the scales: Behind the dead is a barrier (barzakh) until the day they are raised; The damned had taken the believers as a laughingstock; now the believers triumph; God tells the damned pleading to leave hell: 'Be driven away into it and do not speak to me'; At death the sinner begs 'My Lord, send me back, that I may do good'; it is refused; When the trumpet is blown there will be no ties of kinship between them, nor will they ask after one another; Seek refuge in God from the goadings of the devils and from their presence; The dead cannot come back to life on earth; A dying person's plea to God for more life, and God's answer [contrast between the texts]; On that day a great shofar will be blown and the lost in Assyria and outcasts in Egypt will come and worship on the holy mountain; A span of many years is set against a single day [divergence between the texts]; At the judgment after death a whole lifetime is reckoned as an hour or a day; The dead cannot go back to the life they left [divergence between the texts]; and 10 more.

leads.title: Job - cosmic power of God and the impossible lawsuit ↔ Who owns the earth? The fables of the ancients and the impossibility of many gods

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Sufferer imagines suing God but knows God's might would silence or condemn him (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in Job - cosmic power of God and the impossible lawsuit: God made the constellations Ash (Bear?), Kesil (Orion) and Kimah (Pleiades) and the chambers of the south; Life's days flee faster than a runner, reed boats, or a swooping eagle; The earth is given into the hand of the wicked; God covers the faces of its judges; 'He destroys both the blameless and the wicked'; God mocks the calamity of the innocent; God passes by the speaker and he does not see him; God commands the sun not to rise and seals up the stars; God treads on the back (bamot) of Sea; The helpers of Rahab bow beneath God's wrath; 'How can a man be in the right with God? He could not answer one in a thousand'; Lament that there is no umpire (mokhiach) to lay his hand on both God and man; Even if washed in snow and lye, God would plunge him into the pit so his clothes abhor him; God is not questioned about what he does, but they are questioned; and 7 more.

Only in Who owns the earth? The fables of the ancients and the impossibility of many gods: Those called God's offspring are rather honored servants who do not speak before him; The hearing ear and the seeing eye, YHWH made them both; Were there gods besides God in heaven and earth, both would have been ruined; Wonder done 'so that you may know that the earth belongs to YHWH'; 'To whom will you liken God, what likeness compare to him?'; God fashions seven heavens; If asked who created heaven and earth and sends rain, the idolaters themselves answer 'God'; Whether God has a son, or calls his anointed king his begotten son [contrast between the texts]; Heaven and the heaven of heavens belong to God; Unbelievers dismiss the revelation as 'tales of the ancients' (asatir al-awwalin) they could equal; I kill and I make alive, I wound and I heal; there is no god beside me; Declaration that YHWH is God and there is no other besides him.

leads.title: Redemption of land, interest-free loans, and Israelite bondmen ↔ Moses and Aaron rejected; the son of Mary and his mother on a height

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Whose slaves or servants the Israelites are [contrast between the texts] (weight 7.7); Israelites cannot be sold as slaves because they are God's servants whom he brought out of Egypt (weight 7.3). Pair score 15.1.

Only in Redemption of land, interest-free loans, and Israelite bondmen: An impoverished Israelite sold to a brother serves as a hired worker, not a slave, until the jubilee; Houses in Levite cities can always be redeemed and their fields never sold; Do not rule over a fellow Israelite with harshness (perekh); Permanent slaves may be bought from surrounding nations and resident aliens and bequeathed; A house in a walled city can be redeemed only within a year and does not return at the jubilee; Freeing or buying back the enslaved [divergence between the texts]; Sold land returns to its ancestral owner in the jubilee; Israelite sold to a resident alien may be redeemed by kin or himself, priced by years to jubilee; To whom and how widely the ban on interest applies [divergence between the texts]; Lending at interest or increase to a poor brother is forbidden; Nearest kinsman (go'el) has the right and duty to redeem land and family.

Only in Moses and Aaron rejected; the son of Mary and his mother on a height: God gave Mary and her son refuge on a height (rabwa) with a resting place and a flowing spring; The prophet's people object that he is only a human like them; had God willed he would have sent angels; God sends Moses and Aaron together, with his signs, to Pharaoh; Psalm retells Israel's sacred history (patriarchs, Egypt, wilderness, conquest) as instruction or praise; A spring or stream appears for the mother.

leads.title: Sayings on wine, the king's throne and the lamp of YHWH ↔ Who owns the earth? The fables of the ancients and the impossibility of many gods
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: The hearing ear and the seeing eye, YHWH made them both (weight 7.3). Pair score 7.3.

Only in Sayings on wine, the king's throne and the lamp of YHWH: Bruising wounds scour away evil; blows cleanse the inner chambers; Bread gained by deceit is sweet, but afterwards the mouth is filled with gravel; 'Bad, bad,' says the buyer, then goes away and boasts; Counsel in a man's heart is deep water; a man of understanding draws it out; He who curses father or mother, his lamp is put out in the pupil of darkness; Many proclaim their loyalty, but a faithful man who can find?; The breath (nishmat) of man is the lamp of YHWH, searching all the inner chambers of the belly; A wise king winnows the wicked and drives the threshing wheel over them; It is a snare to say rashly 'Holy!' and only afterwards to reflect on vows; The glory of young men is their strength, the splendor of the old their grey hair; Wine is a mocker and strong drink a brawler; whoever is led astray by it is not wise; A king seated on the throne of judgment winnows all evil with his eyes; and 19 more.

Only in Who owns the earth? The fables of the ancients and the impossibility of many gods: Sufferer imagines suing God but knows God's might would silence or condemn him; Those called God's offspring are rather honored servants who do not speak before him; Were there gods besides God in heaven and earth, both would have been ruined; Wonder done 'so that you may know that the earth belongs to YHWH'; 'To whom will you liken God, what likeness compare to him?'; God fashions seven heavens; If asked who created heaven and earth and sends rain, the idolaters themselves answer 'God'; Whether God has a son, or calls his anointed king his begotten son [contrast between the texts]; Heaven and the heaven of heavens belong to God; Unbelievers dismiss the revelation as 'tales of the ancients' (asatir al-awwalin) they could equal; I kill and I make alive, I wound and I heal; there is no god beside me; Declaration that YHWH is God and there is no other besides him.

Only in Proverbs of Solomon copied by Hezekiah's men (king, speech, enemies): A word fitly spoken is like apples of gold in settings of silver; A man without self-restraint is like a city broken into, without walls; Clouds and wind without rain is a man who boasts of a gift he does not give; If you find honey eat only enough, lest you be sated and vomit it; Like the cold of snow in harvest time is a faithful messenger to those who send him; It is the glory of God to conceal a matter and the glory of kings to search it out; Like cold water to a weary soul is good news from a far country; Proverbs of Solomon 'copied out' (he'tiqu) by the men of Hezekiah king of Judah; As heaven for height and earth for depth, so the heart of kings is unsearchable; The north wind brings forth rain, and a backbiting tongue angry looks; A righteous man who gives way before the wicked is like a muddied spring or polluted fountain; Let your foot be seldom in your neighbor's house, lest he grow weary of you and hate you; and 13 more.

leads.title: Psalm 104, the great creation hymn (cf. the Great Hymn to the Aten) ↔ A later generation's messenger, the Cry, and messengers in succession
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Human comes from dust and returns to dust (weight 5.9). Pair score 5.9.

Only in Psalm 104, the great creation hymn (cf. the Great Hymn to the Aten): Hymn praising God as creator, describing the ordering of the cosmos and its creatures; Each creature has its God-given habitat: birds in cedars, stork in junipers, ibex in mountains, hyrax in rocks; God rejoices in his works; Leviathan was formed to sport in the sea, or for God to play with; God sends forth his spirit and renews the face of the earth; At God's rebuke and thunder the primeval waters flee from the mountains to their appointed place; God gives wine to gladden the heart of man, oil to make his face shine and bread to sustain him; Self-exhortation 'Bless YHWH, O my soul'; When God takes away their breath creatures die and return to dust; when he sends his spirit they are created; All in heaven and earth ask of him; every day he is engaged in some affair (kull yawm huwa fi sha'n); God takes life and gives it again [divergence between the texts]; God looks at the earth and it trembles, touches the mountains and they smoke; and 40 more.

Only in A later generation's messenger, the Cry, and messengers in succession: God sent his messengers one after another; each was denied and each nation became a tale; A people is seized by the Cry (al-ṣayḥa) and made like flood-scum; Whether those who die and return to dust rise again [contrast between the texts]; Earlier messengers were only men who ate food and were not immortal; Hero asks the deity to judge or destroy his opponents; Your dead shall live, their corpses rise; dwellers in the dust shall awake and sing; Destruction follows the people's rejection of a messenger.

Shared motifs, rarest first: God sends Moses and Aaron together, with his signs, to Pharaoh (weight 7.1); Psalm retells Israel's sacred history (patriarchs, Egypt, wilderness, conquest) as instruction or praise (weight 6.6). Pair score 13.7.

Only in Psalm 105, historical hymn from the patriarchs through Joseph and the exodus: Egypt rejoiced when Israel left, for dread of them had fallen on it; God turned the Egyptians' hearts to hate his people and deal craftily with them; Joseph's feet were hurt in fetters and his neck (nefesh) put in iron until his word came true; God sent a man ahead of them: Joseph, sold as a slave; Joseph was to bind the king's princes at will and teach his elders wisdom; At the exodus not one among the tribes stumbled (or was feeble); God calls the patriarchs his 'anointed ones' and 'prophets' and rebukes kings for their sake ('Touch not my anointed'); God opened the rock and waters gushed and ran as a river in the desert; The ancestors were few in number, sojourners wandering from nation to nation; The chain of patriarchs to whom revelation or covenant passed [divergence between the texts]; The number of signs or plagues in Egypt [divergence between the texts]; A palpable darkness covers the land for three days; and 31 more.

Only in Moses and Aaron rejected; the son of Mary and his mother on a height: God gave Mary and her son refuge on a height (rabwa) with a resting place and a flowing spring; The prophet's people object that he is only a human like them; had God willed he would have sent angels; Whose slaves or servants the Israelites are [contrast between the texts]; Israelites cannot be sold as slaves because they are God's servants whom he brought out of Egypt; A spring or stream appears for the mother.

leads.title: Psalm 139, God's all-knowing presence and the embryo ↔ Man from clay through the stages of the womb; seven paths, water, Sinai's tree, cattle and ships
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: God's eyes saw the speaker's unformed substance (golem); all his days were written in God's book before one of them existed (weight 7.3); Humans created from dust, then a drop (nuṭfa), then a clinging clot (ʿalaqa), then a chewed lump (muḍgha), shaped and unshaped (weight 7.3); God poured the embryo out like milk and curdled it like cheese, clothing it with skin and flesh and knitting bones and sinews (weight 6.8). Pair score 21.5.

Only in Psalm 139, God's all-knowing presence and the embryo: Darkness is not dark to God; night shines like day, darkness and light are alike; 'YHWH, you have searched me and known me': God knows sitting and rising, thoughts from afar, every word before it is spoken; 'Do I not hate those who hate you, YHWH? I hate them with perfect hatred'; 'If I take the wings of the dawn (shahar) and dwell at the far end of the sea, even there your hand leads me'; No soul dies except by God's leave at a term written (kitaban mu'ajjalan); Speaker was made in secret and embroidered (ruqqamti) in the depths of the earth; No calamity befalls the earth or yourselves but it is in a Book before God brings it into being; Nothing wet or dry but is in a clear book; Fleeing from God, or to God [divergence between the texts]; God's knowledge of a person's thoughts and words, from afar or from near [divergence between the texts]; God knows what the earth diminishes of the dead bodies, and with him is a preserving record; Nowhere to flee God's spirit: if I ascend to heaven you are there, if I make my bed in Sheol you are there; and 13 more.

Only in Man from clay through the stages of the womb; seven paths, water, Sinai's tree, cattle and ships: God called 'the best of creators' (aḥsan al-khāliqīn); Cattle are a lesson: God gives drink from what is in their bellies; A tree springing from Mount Sinai (Ṭūr Saynāʾ) yields oil and a relish for eaters; In the womb God makes the lump into bones and clothes the bones with flesh, then makes it another creation; God's crafting of the human body, and what is said to follow from it [divergence between the texts]; Man is made from compacted (clotted) blood and then bones; God makes the fluid (seed) in women into a human and forms the child in its mother's belly; At creation God fixed the weight of the wind, the measure of the waters, a decree for the rain and a way for the thunderbolt; God fashions seven heavens; The speaker too was 'pinched off from clay' (qoratsti), like a figure nipped from a lump of clay; First human shaped from dust, clay or soil.

Only in Psalm 69, the waters have come up to my neck; gall and vinegar: Enemies give the sufferer poison (rosh, gall) for food and vinegar to drink; Curse that the enemy's encampment be desolate with no one dwelling in his tents; Curse that the enemies' table become a trap and snare; Prayer that the pit (be'er) not close its mouth over the sufferer; What God's heavenly book records: names or deeds [divergence between the texts]; Heaven, earth, seas and all that moves in them praise God; God keeps a book in which names are written and from which sinners are blotted [divergence between the texts]; Speaker fasts and wears sackcloth and becomes a byword and the song of drunkards; The record of the wicked is in Sijjin, that of the righteous in 'Illiyyun, each an inscribed book (kitab marqum) witnessed by those brought near [divergence between the texts]; Zeal for God's house consumes the speaker; Sufferer sinks in deep mire and floodwaters up to the neck, the underworld deep; Prayer that God rebuild the walls of Jerusalem/Zion; and 5 more.

Only in One community split into sects; the heedless rich and the God-fearing: Nation pictured as a body beaten from sole of foot to head, with untended wounds and sores; Humanity was one community (umma) but split its affair into sects; Whether a prophet takes payment for his message [contrast between the texts]; Were there gods besides God in heaven and earth, both would have been ruined; False prophets prophesy 'from their own heart', following their own spirit, having seen nothing; Refrain listing plagues (famine, drought, blight, locust, pestilence, war, overthrow): 'yet you did not return to me'; God did not send the prophets who promise peace; they prophesy a lying vision, divination and the deceit of their heart; God burdens no soul beyond its capacity; Speaker is troubled by the prosperity and ease of the wicked (theodicy); Officers call the visiting prophet 'this madman' (meshugga'); The Prophet asks no wage for the message.

leads.title: Psalm 78, Asaph's historical recital from Egypt to David ↔ Moses and Aaron rejected; the son of Mary and his mother on a height
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Psalm retells Israel's sacred history (patriarchs, Egypt, wilderness, conquest) as instruction or praise (weight 6.6). Pair score 6.6.

Only in Psalm 78, Asaph's historical recital from Egypt to David: God sends a band (mishlahat) of 'evil angels' (mal'akhei ra'im) to execute his wrath; Manna called 'bread of the mighty ones' (lehem abbirim), i.e. food of angels; God struck his enemies backward/in the rear (read by rabbis as the Philistines' hemorrhoids); The exodus wonders are located in 'the field of Zoan' (Tanis); The Lord awakes as from sleep like a warrior shouting from wine; God remembers that humans are flesh, a breath that passes and does not return; God rejected the tent of Joseph and tribe of Ephraim and chose Judah and Mount Zion; In the catastrophe young men are consumed by fire, maidens have no wedding song, widows do not lament; God built his sanctuary like the heights (or heavens) and like the earth founded forever; God took David from the sheepfolds, from following the nursing ewes, to shepherd his people; The ark of God is captured by enemies; God commanded the skies and opened the doors (or windows) of heaven; and 40 more.

Only in Moses and Aaron rejected; the son of Mary and his mother on a height: God gave Mary and her son refuge on a height (rabwa) with a resting place and a flowing spring; The prophet's people object that he is only a human like them; had God willed he would have sent angels; Whose slaves or servants the Israelites are [contrast between the texts]; Israelites cannot be sold as slaves because they are God's servants whom he brought out of Egypt; God sends Moses and Aaron together, with his signs, to Pharaoh; A spring or stream appears for the mother.

Only in Noah, the boiling oven, the lost son and al-Judi: Embark: 'in the name of God be its sailing and its mooring'; God commands: 'Earth, swallow your water; sky, withhold!' and the water subsides; Noah reminds God that his son is of his family and God's promise is true; The elite scorn the prophet because only the lowest of them follow him; God answers that the drowned son is not of Noah's family: 'he is a deed not righteous'; The prophet's stories are 'tidings of the unseen' unknown to him and his people before; The ark sails through waves like mountains; The flood hero is blessed after the flood; the content of the blessing [divergence between the texts]; What the flood hero receives when he leaves the vessel [divergence between the texts]; A son who rejects his father's teaching is to be driven away: 'he is not your son, he was not born to you' [divergence between the texts]; The earth is addressed in the vocative and bidden to open, receive or swallow something [shared matter] [divergence between the texts]; What God says of later generations after the flood: no repeat, or punishment to come [contrast between the texts]; and 35 more.

Only in Noah called a madman; the ark and the boiling oven: God forbids the prophet to address him on behalf of those who did wrong: they will be drowned; The flood hero prays to be landed at a blessed landing place; What the flood hero does when the vessel comes to rest [divergence between the texts]; The flood hero is told he is only a man like the speaker(s) [divergence between the texts]; When and from where the flood waters come [divergence between the texts]; The prophet's people object that he is only a human like them; had God willed he would have sent angels; Whether the flood hero speaks to his people before the flood [divergence between the texts]; Why God destroyed a generation or a people [divergence between the texts]; Who is saved with the hero from the destruction, and why [divergence between the texts]; Hero asks the deity to judge or destroy his opponents; Officers call the visiting prophet 'this madman' (meshugga').

فَقَالَ ٱلْمَلَؤُا۟ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ مِن قَوْمِهِۦ مَا هَٰذَآ إِلَّا بَشَرٌ مِّثْلُكُمْ يُرِيدُ أَن يَتَفَضَّلَ عَلَيْكُمْ وَلَوْ شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ لَأَنزَلَ مَلَٰٓئِكَةً مَّا سَمِعْنَا بِهَٰذَا فِىٓ ءَابَآئِنَا ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ
إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا رَجُلٌۢ بِهِۦ جِنَّةٌ فَتَرَبَّصُوا۟ بِهِۦ حَتَّىٰ حِينٍ

sides.note: In Genesis Noah never speaks before the flood: wa-yyaʿaś Nōaḥ kə-khōl ʾăšer ṣiwwâ ʾōtô; he is chosen because God saw him righteous (ʾōtəkā rāʾîtî ṣaddîq). In the Quran he is a messenger (arsalnā Nūḥan ilā qawmihi) who preaches 'yā qawmi ʿbudū llāha mā lakum min ilāhin ghayruhu', and the chiefs answer that he is only a man like them, possessed (bihi jinna).

فَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُونِ

sides.note: Genesis' Noah obeys in silence (wa-yyaʿaś Nōaḥ kə-khōl ʾăšer ṣiwwâ ʾōtô ʾĕlōhîm) and is never sent to anyone; the Quran's Noah is 'their brother' and 'a trustworthy messenger' (akhūhum ... rasūlun amīn) who asks no wage, and his people 'denied the messengers' (kadhdhabat qawmu Nūḥin al-mursalīn).

leads.title: tannūr: the oven that boiled at the Flood
leads.summary: Akkadian tinūru (oven) reached Aramaic, Hebrew, and Arabic. In the Quran's Noah narrative the sign of the Flood is that the tannūr boiled over.

passages.text: حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا جَآءَ أَمْرُنَا وَفَارَ ٱلتَّنُّورُ قُلْنَا ٱحْمِلْ فِيهَا مِن كُلٍّ زَوْجَيْنِ ٱثْنَيْنِ وَأَهْلَكَ إِلَّا مَن سَبَقَ عَلَيْهِ ٱلْقَوْلُ وَمَنْ ءَامَنَ وَمَآ ءَامَنَ مَعَهُۥٓ إِلَّا قَلِيلٌ

فَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَيْهِ أَنِ ٱصْنَعِ ٱلْفُلْكَ بِأَعْيُنِنَا وَوَحْيِنَا فَإِذَا جَآءَ أَمْرُنَا وَفَارَ ٱلتَّنُّورُ فَٱسْلُكْ فِيهَا مِن كُلٍّ زَوْجَيْنِ ٱثْنَيْنِ وَأَهْلَكَ إِلَّا مَن سَبَقَ عَلَيْهِ ٱلْقَوْلُ مِنْهُمْ وَلَا تُخَٰطِبْنِى فِى ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوٓا۟ إِنَّهُم مُّغْرَقُونَ

evidence.text: The loan chain is established. The motif link (a hot or boiling flood) is the lead to investigate.
